rules.name: Temporary files (your account)
rules.why: The per-user temporary folder. Apps and Windows write scratch files here and recreate them on demand. Files touched in the last 24 hours are left alone in case they are still in use.
sources: Windows %TEMP% is the documented scratch location (GetTempPath); it is safe to clear of stale files. https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/fileio/getting-the-system-temporary-directory

rules.name: Temporary files (Windows)
rules.why: The machine-wide temporary folder used by Windows and installers. Rebuilt as needed.
sources: %SystemRoot%\Temp is a scratch directory; standard cleanup tools (Disk Cleanup) target it.

rules.name: Thumbnail and icon cache
rules.why: Explorer's thumbnail and icon caches. Windows rebuilds them automatically the next time you browse folders.
sources: thumbcache_*.db / iconcache_*.db are regenerated by Explorer; Disk Cleanup removes them under 'Thumbnails'.

rules.name: Crash dumps
rules.why: Application crash dump files written here by Windows Error Reporting. Only useful while actively debugging a crash.
sources: %LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps is the WER LocalDumps default location. https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/wer/collecting-user-mode-dumps

rules.name: Error reporting queue
rules.why: Queued and archived Windows Error Reporting data for your account. Rebuilt when the next problem is reported.

rules.name: Error reporting queue (machine)
rules.why: Machine-wide Windows Error Reporting queue and archive. Rebuilt when the next problem is reported.

rules.name: Old Windows logs
rules.why: Servicing and setup log files (CBS, DISM, Windows Update) older than 7 days. Diagnostic only; Windows keeps writing fresh ones.
sources: %SystemRoot%\Logs holds CBS/DISM/setup logs; they are rotated and safe to prune once old.

rules.name: DirectX shader cache
rules.why: DirectX's compiled shader cache. Games and apps rebuild it automatically; the first launch afterwards may be slightly slower.
sources: %LOCALAPPDATA%\D3DSCache is the DirectX shader cache; Disk Cleanup lists it as 'DirectX Shader Cache'.

rules.name: Temporary files (all accounts)
rules.why: The temporary folders of every user account on this PC. Each is scratch space rebuilt on demand; files from the last 24 hours are left alone.
sources: Each profile's AppData\Local\Temp mirrors the per-user %TEMP% scratch folder.

rules.name: Windows Update download cache
rules.why: Downloaded Windows Update installers that have already been applied. Windows re-downloads anything it still needs. Moved to Quarantine so it can be restored.
sources: SoftwareDistribution\Download is the Windows Update download cache; it is routinely cleared by resetting the Windows Update components. https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/deployment/update/windows-update-troubleshooting
